disableBodyPruning.description: If true, disables request body pruning for the GET, COPY, HEAD, PURGE, and UNLOCK methods.

disableUrlEncoding.description: If true, disables the percent encoding of auth, path, query, and fragment URL segments.

disabledSystemHeaders.description: Disable the system headers which are added implicitly.

insecureHTTPParser.description: If true, uses an insecure HTTP parser that accepts invalid HTTP headers.

followOriginalHttpMethod.description: If true, redirects with the original HTTP method. Redirects with the GET HTTP method by default.

followAuthorizationHeader.description: If true, retains the `authorization` header when a redirect happens to a different hostname.

protocolVersion.description: The HTTP protocol version to use. Supports the `http1`, `http2`, and `auto` values.

removeRefererHeaderOnRedirect.description: If true, removes the `referer` header when a redirect happens.

tlsPreferServerCiphers.description: If true, uses the server's cipher suite order instead of the client's during negotiation.

tlsDisabledProtocols.description: The SSL and TLS protocol versions to disable during negotiation.

tlsCipherSelection.description: The order of cipher suites that the SSL server profile uses to establish a secure connection.

protocolProfileBehavior.description: The [settings](https://learning.postman.com/docs/sending-requests/create-requests/request-settings/) used to alter the [Protocol Profile Behavior](https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-runtime/blob/develop/docs/protocol-profile-behavior.md) of sending a request.

anyOf.description: The request's URL string.

request.description: The request definition. Include for request items, omit for folder items.

item.description: Nested folder items for deeper folder structures.

tools.name: mcp__postman__createComponent
tools.description:
Creates a component in the team's component library and seeds its first draft with
the content you provide. Use this when a team wants a reusable schema, parameter,
response, or security scheme that specifications can reference instead of redefining.
The component starts active and unpublished: the content lands in its draft only.
Call createComponentVersion afterwards to publish it and make it referenceable.
Do not use this tool to edit an existing component's content; use updateComponentDraft
instead. Requires a Postman Enterprise plan.

tools.name: mcp__postman__createComponentVersion

you supply, making it referenceable by the team's specifications. Labels must be
unique per component. Publishing cannot be undone and the resulting version cannot be
edited — publish another version to supersede it. Archived components cannot be
published; restore them with updateComponent first.
Do not use this tool to save work in progress; use updateComponentDraft instead.
Requires a Postman Enterprise plan.

tools.name: mcp__postman__createEnvironment
tools.description:
Creates an environment.

**Note:**

- The request body size cannot exceed the maximum allowed size of 30MB.
- If you receive an HTTP \`411 Length Required\` error response, manually pass the \`Content-Length\` header and its value in the request header.
- If you do not include the \`workspace\` query parameter, the system creates the environment in the oldest personal Internal workspace you own.
- Only [shared variable](https://learning.postman.com/docs/use/send-requests/variables/variables/#share-variable-values) values can be modified through the Postman API. A shared variable is an environment variable with its value synced and stored in the Postman cloud, and can be accessed by your teammates in the environment's workspace.

tools.name: mcp__postman__createMock
tools.description:
Creates a mock server in a collection.

- Pass the collection UID (ownerId-collectionId), not the bare collection ID.
- If you only have a \`collectionId\`, resolve the UID first:
  1) Prefer GET \`/collections/{collectionId}\` and read \`uid\`, or
  2) Construct \`{ownerId}-{collectionId}\` using ownerId from GET \`/me\`:
    - For team-owned collections: \`ownerId = me.teamId\`
    - For personal collections: \`ownerId = me.user.id\`
- Use the \`workspace\` query to place the mock in a specific workspace. Prefer explicit workspace scoping.

tools.name: mcp__postman__createMockServerResponse
tools.description:
Creates a server response on a mock server. Server responses simulate 5xx server-level failures (e.g. 500, 503) that are agnostic to any specific route — when active, every request to the mock returns this response.

- \`statusCode\` must be a 5xx value (500–599).
- \`body\` is a raw string — pass the response body exactly as the mock should return it (e.g. a JSON string like \`"{\"message\":\"error\"}"\` or plain text).
- \`language\` controls syntax highlighting in the Postman UI (\`json\`, \`xml\`, \`html\`, \`javascript\`, \`text\`). It does not affect the actual response Content-Type — set that via \`headers\` instead.
- \`headers\` is an array of \`{key, value}\` pairs for response headers (e.g. \`[{"key": "Content-Type", "value": "application/json"}]\`).
- You can create multiple server responses per mock, but only one can be active at a time. Creating a response does NOT automatically activate it — call \`updateMock\` with \`config.serverResponseId\` set to the new response's \`id\` to activate it.

tools.description:
Starts an SDK generation job for one language from a collection or a specification.
Returns 202 with a job record — the SDK does not exist yet. Poll getSdk and wait for
\`buildStatus\` to reach \`succeeded\` before trying to download it. The request body
depends on the \`language\` you pick, so send only the properties that language accepts.
One call generates one language; call it once per language rather than expecting a
bundle. Requires a Postman Team or Enterprise plan.

tools.name: mcp__postman__createSpec

[Admins and Super Admins](https://learning.postman.com/docs/collaborating-in-postman/roles-and-permissions/#team-roles) can configure workspace permissions to restrict users and/or user groups from creating workspaces or require approvals for the creation of team workspaces.

tools.name: mcp__postman__detectedSecretsQueries
tools.description:
Searches the secrets Postman's Secret Scanner has detected across the team. Despite
being a POST this only reads — the body carries the query, and an empty body returns
everything. Filter with \`secretTypes\` (IDs from getSecretTypes), \`statuses\`
(\`ACTIVE\`, \`FALSE_POSITIVE\`, \`REVOKED\`, \`ACCEPTED_RISK\`), \`resolved\`, \`workspaceVisibilities\`,
and either \`workspaceIds\` or \`resources\` — those last two are mutually exclusive, and
sending both fails. Page with \`limit\` and \`cursor\`, and pass \`include=meta.total\` when
you need the total count.
Secret values come back obfuscated and hashed, never in full. Use
getDetectedSecretsLocations to find where a specific secret appears. Requires a Postman
Enterprise plan.

(\`ACTIVE\`, \`FALSE_POSITIVE\`, \`REVOKED\`, \`ACCEPTED_RISK\`), \`resolved\`, \`workspaceVisibilities\`,
and either \`workspaceIds\` or \`resources\` — those last two are mutually exclusive, and
sending both fails. Page with \`limit\` and \`cursor\`, and pass \`include=meta.total\` when
you need the total count.
Secret values come back obfuscated and hashed, never in full. Use
getDetectedSecretsLocations to find where a specific secret appears. Requires a Postman
Enterprise plan.

limit.description: The maximum number of rows to return in the response.

cursor.description: The pointer to the first record of the set of paginated results. To view the next response, use the `nextCursor` value for this parameter.

include.description:

- `meta.total` — Include the total records found in the `meta` response object.

since.description: Return only results created since the given time, in [ISO 8601](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3339#section-5.6) format. This value cannot be later than the `until` value. To use `time-numoffset` format, you must use `%2B` URL-encoding for the `+` character.

until.description: Return only results created until this given time, in [ISO 8601](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3339#section-5.6) format. This value cannot be earlier than the `since` value. To use `time-numoffset` format, you must use `%2B` URL-encoding for the `+` character.

items.description:
The secret's resolution status:
- `ACTIVE` — The secret is active.
- `FALSE_POSITIVE` — The discovered secret is not an actual secret.
- `REVOKED` — The secret is valid, but the user rotated their key to resolve the issue.
- `ACCEPTED_RISK` — The Secret Scanner found the secret, but user accepts the risk of publishing it.

resource.description:
Returns metrics and insights for API usage, success, and workspace/team trends in Postman:

- `user` — Data related to individual user activities and engagement within Postman workspaces.
- `team` — Team-level analytics, license consumption, and organizational trends.
- `workspace` — Workspace-level activities, elements, and collaboration patterns.
- `ai` — Analytics related to Agent Mode usage across workspaces, covering user activity, model usage, and credit consumption patterns.
- `api_development` — API development activity metrics that include workspace counts, entity activity by type (collection, flow, mock, specification, sdk), and top entities.
- `api_testing` — API testing metrics such as total test runs, functional test runs (Collection Runner), and performance test runs.
- `api_production` — API production metrics, including monitor run activity and production flow execution activity.
- `api_distribution` — API distribution metrics, such as active workspace counts across distribution channels.
- `api_management` — API management metrics, such as workspace activity, active counts, trends, and top workspaces.

metrics.description:
Filters the response by only the given metrics. The metric must match the given `resource` value.

For a list of metrics and their related `resource` value, call the GET `/analytics-metadata` endpoint.

view.description:
The view type for the analytics data:
  - `detailed` — Return extensive information.
  - `summary` — Return aggregated information.
  - `trend` — Return trend information over a duration.

workspaceType.description: A comma-separated list of `internal`, `public`, and `partner` workspace types to filter the results by.

userId.description: A comma-separated list of user IDs to filter the results by. Only pass this parameter when calling the `user_requests` metric for the `workspace` resource.

duration.description: Filters the response by the given duration.

requestId.description: A comma-separated list of unique request IDs (`userId`-`requestId`) to filter the response by. Only pass this parameter when using the `user_requests` metric.

responseStatus.description: A comma-separated list of HTTP response status codes to filter the results by. Accepts values `100` through `600`. Only pass this parameter when using the `user_requests` metric.

attentionType.description: A comma-separated list of issues types to filter the results by. Attention types provide details about issues users or partners are facing. Accepts the `high_non_200OK_rate_for_partner` and `no_success_on_tried_request` values. Only pass this parameter when using the `needs_attention` metric.

period.description: Filters results for a given period of time (as opposed to a range) for supported views. Use a YEAR-MONTH value for month filtering or YEAR-MONTH-DAY day filtering.

userType.description: Filters results by a specific user type for supported views.

entityType.description: The type of Postman entity to filter results by.

limit.description: The maximum number of rows to return in the response.

offset.description: The zero-based offset of the first item to return.

tools.name: mcp__postman__getContextGraphAsk
tools.description:
Gets a submitted Context Graph ask's status and, once it finishes, its result. Call
this after submitContextGraphAsk with the \`askId\` it returned, and poll while
\`status\` is \`pending\` or \`running\` — leave a few seconds between polls rather than
calling in a tight loop.
\`result\` is only present once \`status\` is \`completed\`; a \`failed\` ask carries a short
\`error\` instead. When reporting a completed ask, treat \`result.answer\` as the prose
summary and \`result.structured\`, \`result.citations\`, and \`result.provenance\` as the
graph data it rests on — cite that evidence rather than presenting the answer on its
own, and say so when \`result.provenance.truncated\` is \`true\`, since the ask hit its
deadline and the answer is partial.

Gets a short-lived signed URL for a generated SDK's zip archive. The response carries a
URL, not the archive — the API deliberately does not stream file contents — and the URL
expires within a few minutes, so fetch it at the moment you intend to download and do
not store or pass it around.
Only works once the SDK's \`buildStatus\` is \`succeeded\`; check with getSdk first, since
asking too early returns 409. Requires a Postman Team or Enterprise plan.

tools.name: mcp__postman__getSdkGitConnectionPullRequests
tools.description:
Lists the SDK-update pull requests opened through one Git connection. Use this to report
on what has been delivered to a repository and what is still waiting to be merged. The
record survives disconnection, so a disconnected connection still returns its history.
These are pull requests in the connected Git repository, not Postman collection pull
requests — use getCollectionPullRequests for those. Requires a Postman Team or
Enterprise plan.

tools.name: mcp__postman__getSdks
tools.description:
Lists the SDKs the caller can see in a workspace, with each one's build status.
\`workspaceId\` is required. Filter with \`buildStatus\`, \`language\`, and \`sourceId\`, or

Use \`sdkIds\` here rather than calling getSdk in a loop when you are polling more than
one generation job. Requires a Postman Team or Enterprise plan.

tools.name: mcp__postman__getWorkspace
tools.description:
Gets information about a workspace.

**Note:**

This endpoint's response contains the \`visibility\` field. [Visibility](https://learning.postman.com/docs/collaborating-in-postman/using-workspaces/managing-workspaces/#changing-workspace-visibility) determines who can access the workspace:
- \`personal\` — Only you can access the workspace.
- \`team\` — All team members can access the workspace.
- \`private\` — Only invited team members can access the workspace ([**Team** and **Enterprise** plans only](https://www.postman.com/pricing)).
- \`public\` — Everyone can access the workspace.
- \`partner\` — Only invited team members and [partners](https://learning.postman.com/docs/collaborating-in-postman/using-workspaces/partner-workspaces/) can access the workspace ([**Team** and **Enterprise** plans only](https://www.postman.com/pricing)).

tools.name: mcp__postman__getWorkspaces
tools.description:
Gets all workspaces you have access to.
- For “my ...” requests, first call GET \`/me\` and pass \`createdBy={me.user.id}\`.
- This endpoint's response contains the visibility field. Visibility determines who can access the workspace:
  - \`personal\` — Only you can access the workspace.
  - \`team\` — All team members can access the workspace.
  - \`private\` — Only invited team members can access the workspace (Professional and Enterprise).
  - \`public\` — Everyone can access the workspace.
  - \`partner\` — Invited team members and partners (Professional and Enterprise).
- For tools that require the workspace ID, and no workspace ID is provided, ask the user to provide the workspace ID. If the user does not provide the workspace ID, call this first with the createdBy parameter to use the first workspace.
- Results are paginated. Use the \`cursor\` parameter to retrieve additional pages.
- Examples:
  - “List my workspaces” → GET \`/me\`, then GET \`/workspaces?createdBy={me.user.id}&limit=100\`
  - “List my personal workspaces” → GET \`/me\`, then GET \`/workspaces?type=personal&createdBy={me.user.id}&limit=100\`
  - “List all public workspaces” → GET \`/workspaces?type=public&limit=100\`

  - \`personal\` — Only you can access the workspace.
  - \`team\` — All team members can access the workspace.
  - \`private\` — Only invited team members can access the workspace (Professional and Enterprise).
  - \`public\` — Everyone can access the workspace.
  - \`partner\` — Invited team members and partners (Professional and Enterprise).
- For tools that require the workspace ID, and no workspace ID is provided, ask the user to provide the workspace ID. If the user does not provide the workspace ID, call this first with the createdBy parameter to use the first workspace.
- Results are paginated. Use the \`cursor\` parameter to retrieve additional pages.
- Examples:
  - “List my workspaces” → GET \`/me\`, then GET \`/workspaces?createdBy={me.user.id}&limit=100\`
  - “List my personal workspaces” → GET \`/me\`, then GET \`/workspaces?type=personal&createdBy={me.user.id}&limit=100\`
  - “List all public workspaces” → GET \`/workspaces?type=public&limit=100\`

type.description:
The type of workspace to filter the response by. One of: `personal`, `team`, `private`, `public`, `partner`.
- For “my ...” requests, this can be combined with `createdBy`. If type is not specified, it will search across all types for that user.

createdBy.description:
Return only workspaces created by the specified Postman user ID.
- For “my ...” requests, set `createdBy` to the current user’s ID from GET `/me` (`me.user.id`).
- If the user's ID is not known, first call GET `/me`, then retry with `createdBy`.

include.description:
Include the following information in the endpoint's response:
- `mocks:deactivated` — Include all deactivated mock servers in the response.
- `scim` — Return the SCIM user IDs of the workspace creator and who last modified it.

elementType.description: Filter results to return the workspace where the given element type is located. If you pass this query parameter, you must also pass the `elementId` query parameter.

elementId.description: Filter results to return the workspace where the given element's ID is located. When filtering by collection, you must use the collection's unique ID (`userId`-`collection`). If you pass this query parameter, you must also pass the `elementType` query parameter.

cursor.description: The cursor to get the next set of results in a paginated response. Get this value from the `meta.nextCursor` field in the previous response.

tools.name: mcp__postman__managePartnerWorkspaceInvites
tools.description:
Manages Partner Workspace access: invites partners by email address, removes them from
one workspace, or removes them from the partnership and every workspace in it. Existing
partners are added directly; new email addresses are sent an invitation.
Two of these three actions are broad and irreversible in effect — removing someone from
a partnership revokes their access to every shared workspace at once, not just the one
you were looking at. Confirm the scope before calling, and only act on an explicit
instruction naming the addresses and the action. Inviting sends real email to external
people, so never invite speculatively or to an address you inferred. Requires a Team or
Enterprise plan, and the Partner Manager, Workspace Editor, or Admin role depending on
the action.

tools.description:
Adds or removes roles in bulk for users, groups, teams, and organizations within a team.
Removing a role from a group or a team strips that role's permissions from every member
of it at once, so the blast radius is much larger than the size of the request body.
This changes who can do what. Only call it on an explicit instruction naming the
entities and roles involved, and read the current state with getTeam
(\`include=userRoles\`) first so you can describe what will change.

tools.name: mcp__postman__patchCollection
tools.description:
Updates specific collection information, such as its name, events, or its variables. For more information, see the [Postman Collection Format documentation](https://schema.postman.com/collection/json/v2.1.0/draft-07/docs/index.html).

**Important usage notes:**

- **Sequential calls only.** Do NOT call \`patchCollection\` in parallel with other \`patchCollection\` calls for the same collection — concurrent PATCH requests conflict with each other and cause cancellation errors. Always wait for one call to complete before making another.
- **Partial updates.** Only include the fields you want to change. Omit all other fields entirely; unspecified fields are left unchanged.
- **Variables (\`collection.variable\`).** Send \`key\` and \`value\` for each variable, and use \`disabled\` to turn one off. An \`enabled\` field is accepted but silently ignored, so \`disabled\` is the only one that takes effect.
- **Secret variables.** You can't set secret variables through this endpoint. Manage cloud- or vault-backed secrets through environments instead.
- **Events (\`collection.events\`).** Each event's \`script.id\` is required and must be supplied by you — generate a UUID string for it. Omitting it fails with \`Parameters required: ('id') for key: 'collection.events.script'\`. The event itself is identified by its \`script.id\`.

tools.name: mcp__postman__patchEnvironment

**Note:**

- You can only perform one type of operation at a time. For example, you cannot perform an \`add\` and \`replace\` operation in the same call.
- The request body size cannot exceed the maximum allowed size of 30MB.
- If you receive an HTTP \`411 Length Required\` error response, manually pass the \`Content-Length\` header and its value in the request header.
- To add a description to an existing variable, use the \`add\` operation.
- Only [shared variable](https://learning.postman.com/docs/use/send-requests/variables/variables/#share-variable-values) values can be modified through the Postman API. A shared variable is an environment variable with its value synced and stored in the Postman cloud, and can be accessed by your teammates in the environment's workspace.

tools.name: mcp__postman__publishDocumentation
tools.description:
Publishes a collection's documentation. This makes it publicly available to anyone with the link to the documentation.

**Note:**

- Your [Postman plan](https://www.postman.com/pricing/) impacts your use of these endpoints:
  - For **Free** and **Solo** users, you must have permissions to edit the collection.
  - If [API Governance and Security](https://learning.postman.com/docs/api-governance/configurable-rules/configurable-rules-overview/) is enabled for your [**Enterprise**](https://www.postman.com/pricing/) team, only users with the [Community Manager role](https://learning.postman.com/docs/collaborating-in-postman/roles-and-permissions/#team-roles) can publish documentation.
- Publishing is only supported for collections with HTTP requests.
- You cannot publish a collection added to an API.

tools.name: mcp__postman__putCollection
tools.description:
Replaces the contents of a collection using the [Postman Collection v2.1.0 schema format](https://schema.postman.com/collection/json/v2.1.0/draft-07/docs/index.html). Include the collection's ID values in the request body. If you do not, the endpoint removes the existing items and creates new items.

- To perform an update asynchronously, use the \`Prefer\` header with the \`respond-async\` value. When performing an async update, this endpoint returns a HTTP \`202 Accepted\` response.
- For a complete list of properties and information, see the [Postman Collection Format documentation](https://schema.postman.com/collection/json/v2.1.0/draft-07/docs/index.html).
- For protocol profile behavior, refer to Postman's [Protocol Profile Behavior documentation](https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-runtime/blob/develop/docs/protocol-profile-behavior.md).

**Note:**

- The maximum collection size this endpoint accepts cannot exceed 100 MB.
- Use the GET \`/collection-updates-tasks/{taskId}\` endpoint to get the collection's update status when performing an asynchronous update.
- If you don't include the collection items' ID values from the request body, the endpoint **removes** the existing items and recreates the items with new ID values.
- To copy another collection's contents to the given collection, remove all ID values before you pass it in this endpoint. If you do not, this endpoint returns an error. These values include the \`id\`, \`uid\`, and \`postman_id\` values.

A shared variable is an environment variable with its value synced and stored in the Postman cloud, and can be accessed by your teammates in the environment's workspace.

tools.name: mcp__postman__removeTeamMembers
tools.description:
Removes users, groups, or organizations from a Postman team. Returns 204 with no body on
success.
This is destructive and not self-reversing: removed members lose access to the team's
collections, environments, and workspaces, and restoring them means re-inviting them and
rebuilding their roles. Only call it on an explicit instruction naming exactly who to
remove. Never call it to tidy up inactive members, to act on a list you assembled
yourself, or as a step in some larger cleanup.

tools.name: mcp__postman__runMonitor
tools.description:
Runs a monitor and returns its run results.

**Note:**

- If you pass the \`async=true\` query parameter, the response does not return the \`stats\`, \`executions\`, and \`failures\` responses. To get this information for an asynchronous run, call the GET \`/monitors/{id}\` endpoint.
- If the call exceeds 300 seconds, the endpoint returns an HTTP \`202 Accepted\` response. Use the GET \`/monitors/{id}\` endpoint to check the run's status in the response's \`lastRun\` property. To avoid this, it is recommended that you include the \`async=true\` query parameter when using this endpoint.

tools.name: mcp__postman__submitContextGraphAsk
tools.description:
Asks a natural-language question about the team's software estate — which APIs and
services exist, what they expose, and how they depend on each other — and gets an
answer grounded in the team's Context Graph. Use this for questions about the estate
as a whole that no single collection or workspace can answer.
This is asynchronous and does not return the answer: it returns an \`askId\` with
status \`pending\`. Poll getContextGraphAsk with that ID until \`status\` is \`completed\`
or \`failed\`, and only report an answer once it is \`completed\`. Set
\`includeAnswer=false\` when you want just the graph data and intend to phrase the
answer yourself, and lower \`maxSteps\` (1-15, default 10) to cap how much work the
ask does.
Do not use this tool to search Postman elements by name; use searchPostmanElements
instead. Each ask counts against the team's quota, so ask one well-formed question
rather than retrying variations of the same one. Requires Context Graph to be
enabled for the team.

not the destination loses it on transfer, so people can silently lose access to the

only call this on an explicit instruction naming both teams.

transferWorkspaceElement.

published versions accessible) or restore it (\`active\`). Send only one of the two per

Do not use this tool to change a component's content; use updateComponentDraft instead.
Requires a Postman Enterprise plan.

tools.name: mcp__postman__updateDetectedSecretResolutions
tools.description:
Records how a detected secret was dealt with, in one workspace. Requires \`workspaceId\`
and a \`resolution\` of \`FALSE_POSITIVE\` (not really a secret), \`REVOKED\` (was real, key
has been rotated), or \`ACCEPTED_RISK\` (real, exposure accepted).
This only records a judgement — it does not revoke a credential, remove the secret from
the collection, or make the exposure safe. Never mark something \`REVOKED\` unless the
key has actually been rotated, and never mark it \`ACCEPTED_RISK\` on a person's behalf:
both are decisions a human owner has to make. Requires a Postman Enterprise plan.

schema.name: mcp__postman__updateDetectedSecretResolutions

Records how a detected secret was dealt with, in one workspace. Requires \`workspaceId\`
and a \`resolution\` of \`FALSE_POSITIVE\` (not really a secret), \`REVOKED\` (was real, key
has been rotated), or \`ACCEPTED_RISK\` (real, exposure accepted).
This only records a judgement — it does not revoke a credential, remove the secret from
the collection, or make the exposure safe. Never mark something \`REVOKED\` unless the
key has actually been rotated, and never mark it \`ACCEPTED_RISK\` on a person's behalf:
both are decisions a human owner has to make. Requires a Postman Enterprise plan.

resolution.description:
The secret's resolution status:
- `ACTIVE` — The secret is active.
- `FALSE_POSITIVE` — The discovered secret is not an actual secret.
- `REVOKED` — The secret is valid, but the user rotated their key to resolve the issue.
- `ACCEPTED_RISK` — The Secret Scanner found the secret, but user accepts the risk of publishing it.

workspaceId.description: The ID of the workspace that contains the secret.

tools.name: mcp__postman__updateSdkGitConnection
tools.description:
Changes an SDK Git connection's lifecycle status. Setting \`active\` connects or
reconnects the repository and resumes auto-update pull requests; \`disconnected\` stops
any further pull requests being opened while preserving the historical record, which
stays queryable through getSdkGitConnectionPullRequests. The call is idempotent, so
setting current values is a harmless no-op.
The \`inaccessible\` status is set by Postman and cannot be assigned here — seeing it
means the repository or its credentials need attention on the Git side.
\`autoUpdatePullRequestsEnabled\` is Enterprise-only and is forced to false on Team
plans. Requires a Postman Team or Enterprise plan.

schema.description:
Changes an SDK Git connection's lifecycle status. Setting \`active\` connects or
reconnects the repository and resumes auto-update pull requests; \`disconnected\` stops
any further pull requests being opened while preserving the historical record, which
stays queryable through getSdkGitConnectionPullRequests. The call is idempotent, so
setting current values is a harmless no-op.
The \`inaccessible\` status is set by Postman and cannot be assigned here — seeing it
means the repository or its credentials need attention on the Git side.
\`autoUpdatePullRequestsEnabled\` is Enterprise-only and is forced to false on Team
plans. Requires a Postman Team or Enterprise plan.

autoUpdatePullRequestsEnabled.description:
If true, pull requests are opened automatically whenever the source changes or a new version of the SDK generator is released. If false, pull requests are opened automatically, but only for manually-triggered SDK regeneration. If `autoUpdatePullRequestsEnabled` isn't set, the default behavior depends on the user's Postman plan:

- **Enterprise** plan users — Defaults to the `true` value.
- **Team** plan users and read only — Defaults to the `false` value.

- This endpoint does not accept an empty request body. You must pass one of the accepted values.
- This endpoint does not accept multiple request body properties in a single call. For example, you cannot pass both the \`content\` and \`type\` property at the same time.
- Multi-file specifications can only have one root file.
- When updating a file type to \`ROOT\`, the previous root file is updated to the \`DEFAULT\` file type.
- Files cannot exceed a maximum of 10 MB in size.

tools.description:
Changes who can access a workspace, for users, user groups, or partners. Read the
current state with getWorkspaceRoles first and get assignable role names from
getAllWorkspaceRoles.
Several constraints will reject an otherwise reasonable call: at most 50 operations per
request, exactly one action per user, group, or partner in a body, and partner roles and
user roles cannot be changed in the same call. Personal workspaces do not support role
assignment, the external Guest role is not supported, and user groups require an
Enterprise plan. Pass the \`identifierType=scim\` header to use SCIM IDs.
This grants or removes access to everything in the workspace, so only call it on an
explicit instruction naming the people and roles involved.

from.content: A keeper (a free external cron calling our /api/keeper endpoint) calls

target.text: every minute; the dashboard also has a Reclaim button

from.content: every minute; the dashboard and MCP server also reclaim on open, and there's a Reclaim button

A contract can't act on a timer by itself, so expiry refunds need a trigger. Anyone can call `reclaimExpired`, and the money can only ever go to the owner, so the keeper needs no special rights: it is a wallet with a little MON, and if it stops, the owner can still reclaim from the dashboard or the MCP server. We don't need a VM: [cron-job.org](https://cron-job.org) (free, every minute) calls a secret-protected Vercel endpoint, with a local cron as backup.

target.text: App log, linked to the mandate

from.content: Local log (MCP: a file on the user's machine; web: browser storage)
Local log + mint transaction

Money events live on-chain and the agent's working notes live with the user, so no central server holds the log.

- **On-chain history.** The contract keeps a short history list per mandate, so the timeline loads with one read. Scanning past events isn't practical: Monad testnet's public RPC only returns events from the last 100 blocks (about 40 seconds) per request.
- **Local step log.** The MCP server writes each step to `~/.taskpay/logs/<mandate id>.jsonl`. The web app saves it in the browser, where it stays until browser data is cleared, with a JSON/CSV export button.
- **Tamper-evident.** When a mandate closes, a hash of the step log is recorded on-chain, so anyone can check the local log against it later.

The timeline merges both, with an explorer link on every on-chain line.

**How the demo shows this:** a careful model like Claude may refuse the injected instruction, which would leave nothing for the contract to stop. So the web demo has a "compromised agent" switch that follows the review's instruction on purpose, and the CLI has a `taskpay attack` command that uses the agent's own key to pay an unknown address. Both show the same point: even a fooled or stolen agent can't pay outside the mandate.

| Function | Who can call it | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createMandate` | Owner | Locks the budget and records the rules |
| `pay` | Agent | Checks the rules, then pays the merchant, or records a block with the reason |
| `requestTopUp` | Agent | Records a request for more budget, with a reason. Moves no money. |
| `increaseBudget` | Owner only | Adds money after the owner approves a top-up |
| `close` | Owner or agent | Ends the task, refunds the rest to the owner and records the step-log hash |
| `reclaimExpired` | Anyone (the keeper) | After expiry, refunds the rest to the owner |
| `freezeAndRefund` | Owner | Stops the agent and refunds every open mandate it holds |
| `getHistory` | Anyone (read-only) | Returns the mandate's history list for the timeline |
| `openExpired` | Anyone (read-only) | Lists expired mandates that still hold money, for the keeper |

I've put your four answers into both copies of the PRD. One more subagent is running, fetching and checking the ERC-8004 reference contracts so we can deploy our own copy on testnet.

## Your 4 points

**1. LLM:** agreed. The MCP server comes first, tested in Claude Code, and the web app calls Claude Sonnet through your LiteLLM gateway. One thing to plan for: the gateway in `litellm/` listens only on your own machine (`127.0.0.1:4000`). Vercel can't reach it there, so before the web agent goes live you'll need to expose it through a tunnel, such as cloudflared or ngrok, protected by the master key.

**2. Hijack demo (my recommendation):**
- The web app gets a **"compromised agent" switch** that follows the injected review on purpose.
- The CLI gets a **`taskpay attack`** command that uses the agent's own key to pay an unknown address.

Both prove the same thing: a fooled or stolen agent still can't pay outside the mandate. Claude stays in charge of the normal happy-path flow.

**3. Where the log lives:** you're right to worry that off-chain means a central entity. So I split it:
- **Money events go on-chain:** payments, blocks, top-ups, refunds, freezes. Nobody controls them.
  - I tested Monad testnet's public RPC: it only returns events from the **last 100 blocks (about 40 seconds)** per request.
  - So the contract itself keeps a short history list per mandate, and the timeline loads with one read instead of scanning events.
- **The agent's working notes stay with the user:**
  - MCP: a file at `~/.taskpay/logs/<id>.jsonl`.
  - Web: the browser's localStorage, which persists until browser data is cleared, plus an export button.
- **When a task closes, a hash of that local log goes on-chain,** so the notes can be checked against it later. No server ever holds them.

**4. Expiry refunds: no VM needed.**
- Anyone can trigger a refund, and the money can only go to the owner. So the job needs no special rights, just a wallet with a little MON.
- Use **[cron-job.org](https://cron-job.org)** (free, runs every minute) to call a secret-protected Vercel endpoint, `/api/keeper`. Your local cron can run as a backup.

The installer worked, but `foundryup` isn't on your `PATH` yet, so the second command in your `&&` chain couldn't find it. (Even if the installer had updated your shell config, that change wouldn't apply to the shell you're already in.)

**Quick fix for this session:**

```bash
export PATH="$PATH:$HOME/.foundry/bin"
foundryup
```

**Permanent fix (zsh, the macOS default):**

```bash
echo 'export PATH="$PATH:$HOME/.foundry/bin"' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc
foundryup
```

If you use bash instead, replace `~/.zshrc` with `~/.bash_profile`.

**Verify the install:**

```bash
forge --version
cast --version
anvil --version
```

If `forge` isn't found after `foundryup` finishes, open a new terminal or run `source ~/.zshrc` again.

  - IdentityRegistry: `0x8004A818BFB912233c491871b3d84c89A494BD9e`. 2100 agents registered.
  - ReputationRegistry: `0x8004B663056A597Dffe9eCcC1965A193B7388713`. Its `getIdentityRegistry` points to the testnet IdentityRegistry above.
  - ValidationRegistry: `0x8004Cb1BF31DAf7788923b405b754f57acEB4272`.
  
  These proxies point to the same implementation addresses as mainnet, with byte-identical code. Owner, `name`, and `getVersion` ("2.0.0") also match mainnet. The ABI is identical, so the app only needs a per-chain address map. Nothing was deployed, signed or sent.
  
  ## Repo, commit, license
  - Repo: https://github.com/erc-8004/erc-8004-contracts. HEAD is `b9e466c250744a7e06b13dff9d3c2844ed64f825` (2026-08-15). The registry contracts were last changed in `27caef926f8529491256da5b86804cf827d44b93` (2026-01-24).
  - The HEAD source matches the verified on-chain source (only a trailing newline differs).
  - License: the repo has no LICENSE file. The README says "CC0", and the SPDX headers in the `.sol` files say MIT. Both are permissive.
  
  ## Proxy and implementation on mainnet (chain 143)
  - Both 0x8004… addresses are OpenZeppelin `ERC1967Proxy` contracts (UUPS upgradeable).
  - The slot given in the task returns 0 because it isn't the EIP-1967 implementation slot. The correct slot is `0x360894a13ba1a3210667c828492db98dca3e2076cc3735a920a3ca505d382bbc`.
  - Implementations:
    - Identity: `0x7274e874CA62410a93Bd8bf61c69d8045E399c02`
    - Reputation: `0x16e0FA7f7C56B9a767E34B192B51f921BE31dA34`
  - `owner()` on both proxies, on both chains, is `0x547289319C3e6aedB179C0b8e8aF0B5ACd062603`. That account can upgrade them.
  
  ## Verification status
  - MonadVision Sourcify: both implementations are `exact_match` on chains 143 and 10143. The mainnet Identity proxy is `match` (ERC1967Proxy).
  - The testnet proxies are not verified on Sourcify. Their bytecode is identical to the verified mainnet proxy.
  - Nothing is verified on sourcify.dev.
  - Compiler (from verified metadata): solc 0.8.24, optimizer on with 200 runs, viaIR, evmVersion shanghai, OpenZeppelin (contracts and contracts-upgradeable) 5.4.0.
  
  ## Files in `/Users/jainam.oswal/Downloads/Temp/Monad-Blitz-v3-2026/vendor/erc-8004/`
  - `contracts/`: `IdentityRegistryUpgradeable.sol`, `ReputationRegistryUpgradeable.sol`, `ERC1967Proxy.sol`, `HardhatMinimalUUPS.sol`, `MinimalUUPS.sol`. I read every file in full and found nothing malicious. Upgrades are owner-gated.
    - Don't reuse `MinimalUUPS.sol` for a deploy of our own: its owner is hard-coded to the official deployer address.
  - `abis/IdentityRegistry.json` and `abis/ReputationRegistry.json`: taken from the verified contracts. The repo's own Identity ABI is out of date (it lacks `isAuthorizedOrOwner`).
  - `PROVENANCE.md`: sources, address table, verification details, dependencies and remappings, initializer rules, and the deploy order if we ever deploy our own.
  - `ABI-NOTES.md`: signatures, selectors, event topics, revert reasons, and how feedback auth works.
  
  ## Key signatures
  **Registering an agent:**
  - Three overloads, each returning `agentId`:
    - `register()` (0x1aa3a008)
    - `register(string agentURI)` (0xf2c298be)
    - `register(string agentURI, (string metadataKey, bytes metadataValue)[] metadata)` (0x8ea42286)
  - Anyone can register. The NFT is minted to the caller with `_safeMint`, so a contract caller must implement `onERC721Received`.
  - `agentId` starts at 0. Get it from the `Registered(uint256 indexed agentId, string agentURI, address indexed owner)` event.
  - The agent card is the `tokenURI`; change it with `setAgentURI(uint256,string)`.
  
  **Metadata:**
  - `setMetadata(uint256 agentId, string metadataKey, bytes metadataValue)`, callable by the owner or an approved address.
  - The key `agentWallet` is reserved. It can only be changed with `setAgentWallet(uint256,address,uint256 deadline,bytes signature)`, which needs an EIP-712 signature from the new wallet. Deadline is at most 5 minutes ahead.
  
  **Giving feedback:**
  - `giveFeedback(uint256 agentId, int128 value, uint8 valueDecimals, string tag1, string tag2, string endpoint, string feedbackURI, bytes32 feedbackHash)` (0x3c036a7e).
  - There is no feedbackAuth and no signature in v2.0.0 (older drafts had one; it was removed). Any address can submit except:
    - The agent's owner and approved operators. They are rejected with "Self-feedback not allowed", so the rater must be a different wallet from the agent owner.
    - Feedback for an agent that doesn't exist reverts.
    - `valueDecimals` must be at most 18 and |value| at most 1e38.
  - Event: `NewFeedback(uint256 indexed agentId, address indexed clientAddress, uint64 feedbackIndex, int128 value, uint8 valueDecimals, string indexed indexedTag1, string tag1, string tag2, string endpoint, string feedbackURI, bytes32 feedbackHash)`.
  
  **Reading reputation:**
  - `getSummary(uint256 agentId, address[] clientAddresses, string tag1, string tag2) returns (uint64 count, int128 summaryValue, uint8 summaryValueDecimals)`. It reverts if `clientAddresses` is empty, so pass the payer addresses we trust.
  - Also available: `readFeedback`, `readAllFeedback`, `getClients(uint256)` and `getLastIndex`.
  
  ## If we ever deploy our own copy
  1. Deploy the `HardhatMinimalUUPS` implementation.
  2. Deploy an Identity proxy pointing at it, initialized with `initialize(address(0))`. The deployer becomes owner.
  3. Deploy a Reputation proxy pointing at it, initialized with `initialize(IdentityProxy)`.
  4. Deploy the two real implementations. Neither takes constructor arguments.
  5. As owner, call `upgradeToAndCall(IdentityImpl, initialize())` on the Identity proxy.
  6. As owner, call `upgradeToAndCall(ReputationImpl, initialize(IdentityProxy))` on the Reputation proxy.
  
  The proxy can't be pointed straight at the real implementations because their `initialize` functions are `reinitializer(2) onlyOwner`.
  
  ## Compile result
  Not done: Foundry (forge) and solc aren't installed locally, and I didn't install anything. Since both implementations are exact-match verified with the same source, compiler and settings, the source is confirmed to build. For Foundry you would need remappings for `@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/` and `@openzeppelin/contracts/` (OpenZeppelin v5.4.0) and `via_ir = true`.
  
  ## Not verified
  - I did not compile locally.
  - Whether viaIR is strictly required (I copied the setting from the upstream config).
  - Who controls the owner address `0x5472…2603`. It can upgrade the official contracts.
  - The official docs page doesn't label its addresses as mainnet or testnet; the testnet pair comes from the repo README plus my on-chain checks.
  - Function selectors were computed with my own pure-Python Keccak script and spot-checked against the known `Transfer` topic and `tokenURI` selector.

Atlassian MCP server. Three layers of tools:

Only call with an operation `name` from discover results or one already in your tool list; never guess, assume, or invent a name — when unsure, call discover first.

cloudId:
- If YOUR client session has no site context, call getAccessibleAtlassianResources ONCE and reuse the returned cloudId. On any execute-family call, always pass cloudId as a TOP-LEVEL argument (sibling of `name`/`inputs`), never inside `inputs`.

## atlassian
Atlassian MCP server. Three layers of tools:
1. Primary tools (e.g. getJiraIssue, searchJiraIssuesUsingJql, searchConfluence, getConfluenceContent) are already in your tool list. Call them directly.
2. `discover` — when you do not know an operation's name, describe the goal. Returns `results` (each with the exact `name` + `inputs` + the matching execute-family tool for read/write/destructive operations). Do not discover an operation you already have as a primary tool.
3. Run a discovered operation with the execute-family tool matching its risk tier: `executeRead({ name, cloudId, inputs })` for read-only lookups, `executeWrite({ name, cloudId, inputs })` for non-destructive creates/updates, `executeDestructive({ name, cloudId, inputs })` for deletes/irreversible changes. Only call with an operation `name` from discover results or one already in your tool list; never guess, assume, or invent a name — when unsure, call discover first.

cloudId:
- If YOUR client session has no site context, call getAccessibleAtlassianResources ONCE and reuse the returned cloudId. On any execute-family call, always pass cloudId as a TOP-LEVEL argument (sibling of `name`/`inputs`), never inside `inputs`.

Other context:
- The current user's accountId is available from `atlassianUserInfo`.
- Slim large responses with `responseFields` (dot paths) or a `view` preset (compact/evidence/full).

# Jira custom fields (story points, etc.)
Default view is compact — custom fields are omitted unless you pass view: evidence/full, or fields with this site's customfield_* IDs (IDs differ per site). Values appear under fields.customFields, not as top-level customfield_* keys.

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## atlassian
Atlassian MCP server. Three layers of tools:
1. Primary tools (e.g. getJiraIssue, searchJiraIssuesUsingJql, searchConfluence, getConfluenceContent) are already in your tool list. Call them directly.

3. Run a discovered operation with the execute-family tool matching its risk tier: `executeRead({ name, cloudId, inputs })` for read-only lookups, `executeWrite({ name, cloudId, inputs })` for non-destructive creates/updates, `executeDestructive({ name, cloudId, inputs })` for deletes/irreversible changes. # ERC-8004 vendored contracts: provenance

Retrieved 2026-10-10 for TaskPay (Monad Blitz Pune V3). Reference copy only. The official
deployments already exist on **both** Monad mainnet and Monad testnet (see below), so these files
are for reading, ABI reference and local testing. We do not have to deploy them.

## Source

- Repo: https://github.com/erc-8004/erc-8004-contracts
- Commit cloned (HEAD of default branch): `b9e466c250744a7e06b13dff9d3c2844ed64f825` (2026-08-15)
- Last commit touching the two registry contracts: `27caef926f8529491256da5b86804cf827d44b93`
  (2026-01-24, "remove default set"). HEAD contents of both files are identical to the
  **Sourcify exact_match verified source** of the Monad implementations (diff only a trailing newline).
- Contract version: `getVersion()` returns `"2.0.0"` (on-chain on both chains as well).
- Spec: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8004 (Draft). The repo also has a copy in ERC8004SPEC.md, not vendored.

## License

- The repo has **no LICENSE file**. README says "CC0 - Public Domain".
- SPDX headers in the vendored `.sol` files say `MIT`.
- OpenZeppelin dependencies are MIT.
- Either way it is permissive. Keep the SPDX headers as-is.

## Files in this directory

| File | Origin | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `contracts/IdentityRegistryUpgradeable.sol` | repo `contracts/` | ERC-721 agent identity (UUPS) |
| `contracts/ReputationRegistryUpgradeable.sol` | repo `contracts/` | feedback registry (UUPS) |
| `contracts/ERC1967Proxy.sol` | repo `contracts/` | re-export of OZ ERC1967Proxy (the proxy actually deployed) |
| `contracts/HardhatMinimalUUPS.sol` | repo `contracts/` | placeholder impl, owner = msg.sender (use this for a self-deploy) |
| `contracts/MinimalUUPS.sol` | repo `contracts/` | placeholder impl used by official testnet deploy; **owner hard-coded to 0x547289319C3e6aedB179C0b8e8aF0B5ACd062603**, so do NOT use it for our own deploy |
| `abis/IdentityRegistry.json` | Sourcify (MonadVision) verified ABI of impl `0x7274e874...9c02` | authoritative ABI. The repo's `abis/IdentityRegistry.json` is stale: it lacks `isAuthorizedOrOwner` and the ECDSA errors |
| `abis/ReputationRegistry.json` | Sourcify verified ABI of impl `0x16e0fa7f...da34` | identical to repo `abis/ReputationRegistry.json` |

Not vendored: ValidationRegistryUpgradeable.sol (spec still in flux), MinimalUUPSMainnet.sol,
SingletonFactory.sol, plus scripts, tests and hardhat config (not reviewed for execution and not needed).

Review: all Solidity files above were read in full. Nothing malicious was found: no selfdestruct, no
arbitrary delegatecall, no hidden owners other than the documented hard-coded owner in MinimalUUPS.
Upgrades are gated by `onlyOwner` (`_authorizeUpgrade`).

## What is deployed on Monad (checked via RPC 2026-10-10)

Both chains use the same proxy pattern: an OZ `ERC1967Proxy` (Sourcify name
`project/contracts/ERC1967Proxy.sol:ERC1967Proxy`, solc 0.8.24) pointing at a UUPS
implementation. The implementation slot is the standard EIP-1967 slot
`0x360894a13ba1a3210667c828492db98dca3e2076cc3735a920a3ca505d382bbc`.
(The slot ending in `...cc7453e8ddb6ad3f6e0a0f86` returns 0. It is not the EIP-1967 slot.)

| | Monad mainnet (143) | Monad testnet (10143) |
|---|---|---|
| IdentityRegistry proxy | `0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432` | `0x8004A818BFB912233c491871b3d84c89A494BD9e` |
| ReputationRegistry proxy | `0x8004BAa17C55a88189AE136b182e5fdA19dE9b63` | `0x8004B663056A597Dffe9eCcC1965A193B7388713` |
| ValidationRegistry proxy | n/a | `0x8004Cb1BF31DAf7788923b405b754f57acEB4272` (impl `0xdb31f5d9...7f99`) |
| Identity impl | `0x7274e874CA62410a93Bd8bf61c69d8045E399c02` | same address, identical bytecode |
| Reputation impl | `0x16e0FA7f7C56B9a767E34B192B51f921BE31dA34` | same address, identical bytecode |
| owner() (both proxies) | `0x547289319C3e6aedB179C0b8e8aF0B5ACd062603` | same |
| Reputation `getIdentityRegistry()` (slot 0) | `0x8004A169...a432` | `0x8004A818...BD9e` |
| Identity `_lastId` (agents registered) | 0x2858 = 10328 | 0x834 = 2100 |

The 0x8004A169/0x8004BAa1 pair is the **mainnet** vanity set. The 0x8004A818/0x8004B663 pair is
the **testnet** vanity set (same as Sepolia, Base Sepolia, etc.). Both sets were deployed via CREATE2
through the Safe singleton factory `0x914d7Fec6aaC8cd542e72Bca78B30650d45643d7` with different
placeholder salts. Implementations use salts 0x..05 (identity) and 0x..06 (reputation), which is why
the impl addresses are the same on every chain.

**Implication for TaskPay:** use a per-chain address map. The ABI is identical on both networks.
No self-deployment is needed.

## Verification status

MonadVision Sourcify (`https://sourcify-api-monad.blockvision.org/v2/contract/<chain>/<addr>`):
- Identity impl `0x7274...9c02`: chain 143 runtime `exact_match`; chain 10143 creation and runtime `exact_match`.
- Reputation impl `0x16e0...da34`: chain 143 runtime `exact_match`; chain 10143 creation and runtime `exact_match`.
- Mainnet identity proxy `0x8004A169...`: `match` (ERC1967Proxy).
- Testnet proxies `0x8004A818...` and `0x8004B663...`: not verified on Sourcify. Bytecode is byte-identical
  to the verified mainnet proxy runtime, and the impl slot points to the verified impls.
- sourcify.dev (main instance): not verified for any of these addresses.

Compiler settings (from verified metadata): solc `0.8.24+commit.e11b9ed9`, optimizer enabled runs=200,
`viaIR: true`, `evmVersion: shanghai`.

## Dependencies to compile

- `@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable@5.4.0`
- `@openzeppelin/contracts@5.4.0` (ECDSA, IERC1271, ERC1967Proxy)
- Foundry remappings (if used):
  ```
  @openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/=lib/openzeppelin-contracts-upgradeable/contracts/
  @openzeppelin/contracts/=lib/openzeppelin-contracts/contracts/
  ```
  (Use tag v5.4.0 of both OZ repos. The upgradeable repo's own `lib/` submodule also provides the non-upgradeable package.)
- foundry.toml: `solc = "0.8.24"`, `via_ir = true`, `optimizer = true`, `optimizer_runs = 200`, `evm_version = "shanghai"`.
  viaIR is required to avoid stack-too-deep errors in `readAllFeedback` and `getSummary` (UNVERIFIED locally; matches upstream config).

## Upgradeability / initializer requirements (for a self-deploy, if ever needed)

- Both impl constructors call `_disableInitializers()`, so they take no constructor args.
- `IdentityRegistryUpgradeable.initialize()` is `reinitializer(2) onlyOwner`.
- `ReputationRegistryUpgradeable.initialize(address identityRegistry_)` is `reinitializer(2) onlyOwner`.
- Because the initializers are `onlyOwner` at version 2, **you cannot point a fresh proxy straight at
  the real impl**. Owner must first be set by a version-1 placeholder (`HardhatMinimalUUPS.initialize`,
  which runs `__Ownable_init(msg.sender)`). After that, upgrade with `upgradeToAndCall`.
- `ReputationRegistry` stores `_identityRegistry` in plain slot 0. The placeholder writes the same slot.
- Upgrade authority: `owner()` via `_authorizeUpgrade(...) onlyOwner`.

Self-deploy order (testnet, for reference only; the official one already exists):
1. Deploy `HardhatMinimalUUPS` impl (no args) → `M`.
2. Deploy `ERC1967Proxy(M, abi.encodeCall(HardhatMinimalUUPS.initialize, (address(0))))` → `IdP` (owner = deployer EOA).
3. Deploy `ERC1967Proxy(M, abi.encodeCall(HardhatMinimalUUPS.initialize, (IdP)))` → `RepP`.
4. Deploy `IdentityRegistryUpgradeable` impl (no args) → `IdI`; deploy `ReputationRegistryUpgradeable` impl → `RepI`.
5. As owner: `IdP.upgradeToAndCall(IdI, abi.encodeCall(IdentityRegistryUpgradeable.initialize, ()))`.
6. As owner: `RepP.upgradeToAndCall(RepI, abi.encodeCall(ReputationRegistryUpgradeable.initialize, (IdP)))`.
7. Check: `IdP.name()=="AgentIdentity"`, `IdP.getVersion()=="2.0.0"`, `RepP.getIdentityRegistry()==IdP`.

Source of truth: verified implementations on Monad (see PROVENANCE.md) and `abis/*.json` in this dir.
The ABI is the same on mainnet and testnet; only the addresses differ.

| | Monad mainnet (143) | Monad testnet (10143) |
|---|---|---|
| IdentityRegistry | `0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432` | `0x8004A818BFB912233c491871b3d84c89A494BD9e` |
| ReputationRegistry | `0x8004BAa17C55a88189AE136b182e5fdA19dE9b63` | `0x8004B663056A597Dffe9eCcC1965A193B7388713` |

Selectors were computed locally with keccak256. They were sanity-checked against known values for
`Transfer` and `tokenURI`.

## IdentityRegistry (ERC-721 "AgentIdentity"/"AGENT", ERC721URIStorage, EIP-712 domain "ERC8004IdentityRegistry" v"1")

```solidity
struct MetadataEntry { string metadataKey; bytes metadataValue; }

function register() external returns (uint256 agentId);                                   // 0x1aa3a008
function register(string agentURI) external returns (uint256 agentId);                    // 0xf2c298be
function register(string agentURI, MetadataEntry[] metadata) external returns (uint256);  // 0x8ea42286
function setAgentURI(uint256 agentId, string newURI) external;                            // 0x0af28bd3
function tokenURI(uint256 agentId) external view returns (string);                        // 0xc87b56dd
function ownerOf(uint256 agentId) external view returns (address);                        // 0x6352211e
function setMetadata(uint256 agentId, string metadataKey, bytes metadataValue) external;  // 0x466648da
function getMetadata(uint256 agentId, string metadataKey) external view returns (bytes);  // 0xcb4799f2
function getAgentWallet(uint256 agentId) external view returns (address);                 // 0x00339509
function setAgentWallet(uint256 agentId, address newWallet, uint256 deadline, bytes signature) external; // 0x2d1ef5ae
function unsetAgentWallet(uint256 agentId) external;
function isAuthorizedOrOwner(address spender, uint256 agentId) external view returns (bool); // 0xd95e72be
function getVersion() external pure returns (string); // "2.0.0"
```

How it behaves (from source):
- `register*` mints to `msg.sender`. Anyone can call it and there is no fee. `agentId` starts at **0** and
  increments (`_lastId++`). Because of the `register` overloads, viem/ethers need the full signature
  (e.g. `"register(string)"`) or an explicit ABI item. Read `agentId` from the return value of a
  simulated call, or from the `Registered` / `Transfer` event in the receipt.
- `_safeMint` is used. If the caller is a contract, it must implement `onERC721Received`.
- On register, `agentWallet` metadata is set to `msg.sender`. Key `"agentWallet"` is reserved: `setMetadata` and
  the `register` metadata array revert with `"reserved key"` for it.
- `setMetadata` / `setAgentURI` / `setAgentWallet` / `unsetAgentWallet`: the caller must be the owner,
  an operator approved for all, or the token-approved address. Otherwise they revert with `"Not authorized"`.
- `setAgentWallet` signature: an EIP-712 typed-data signature **by `newWallet`** over
  `AgentWalletSet(uint256 agentId,address newWallet,address owner,uint256 deadline)`
  (typehash `0x678b53cd718d595370ab070ebf48edfdcd834beac116bf23e625fc7f4d5b7d32`), with domain
  `{name:"ERC8004IdentityRegistry", version:"1", chainId, verifyingContract: IdentityRegistry proxy}`.
  `owner` is the current token owner. The deadline must satisfy `now <= deadline <= now + 300s`. If ECDSA
  recovery fails, the contract falls back to ERC-1271 `isValidSignature` on `newWallet`.
- Transferring the NFT clears `agentWallet`.
- The agent card / registration file is just the `tokenURI` string (ipfs:// or https:// or data:). Its shape is
  defined in the spec (type, name, description, image, services[], registrations[{agentRegistry, agentId}], supportedTrust[]),
  where `agentRegistry = "eip155:<chainId>:<IdentityRegistry address>"`.

Events:
```solidity
event Registered(uint256 indexed agentId, string agentURI, address indexed owner);
// topic0 0xca52e62c367d81bb2e328eb795f7c7ba24afb478408a26c0e201d155c449bc4a
event MetadataSet(uint256 indexed agentId, string indexed indexedMetadataKey, string metadataKey, bytes metadataValue);
// topic0 0x2c149ed548c6d2993cd73efe187df6eccabe4538091b33adbd25fafdb8a1468b
event URIUpdated(uint256 indexed agentId, string newURI, address indexed updatedBy);
// topic0 0x3a2c7fffc2cba7582c690e3b82c453ea02a308326a98a3ad7576c606336409fb

```

## ReputationRegistry

```solidity
function giveFeedback(
    uint256 agentId,
    int128  value,          // signed fixed-point, |value| <= 1e38
    uint8   valueDecimals,  // 0..18
    string  tag1,           // optional, "" allowed (indexed in event as keccak)
    string  tag2,           // optional
    string  endpoint,       // optional, emitted only (not stored)
    string  feedbackURI,    // optional, emitted only (off-chain feedback JSON)
    bytes32 feedbackHash    // optional, emitted only (keccak of feedbackURI content; 0x0 ok)
) external;                                                                                  // 0x3c036a7e

function revokeFeedback(uint256 agentId, uint64 feedbackIndex) external;                     // 0x4ab3ca99
function appendResponse(uint256 agentId, address clientAddress, uint64 feedbackIndex,
                        string responseURI, bytes32 responseHash) external;                  // 0xc2349ab2

function getSummary(uint256 agentId, address[] clientAddresses, string tag1, string tag2)
    external view returns (uint64 count, int128 summaryValue, uint8 summaryValueDecimals);   // 0x81bbba58
function readFeedback(uint256 agentId, address clientAddress, uint64 feedbackIndex)
    external view returns (int128 value, uint8 valueDecimals, string tag1, string tag2, bool isRevoked); // 0x232b0810
function readAllFeedback(uint256 agentId, address[] clientAddresses, string tag1, string tag2, bool includeRevoked)
    external view returns (address[] clients, uint64[] feedbackIndexes, int128[] values,
                           uint8[] valueDecimals, string[] tag1s, string[] tag2s, bool[] revokedStatuses); // 0xd9d84224
function getClients(uint256 agentId) external view returns (address[]);                       // 0x42dd519c
function getLastIndex(uint256 agentId, address clientAddress) external view returns (uint64); // 0xf2d81759
function getResponseCount(uint256 agentId, address clientAddress, uint64 feedbackIndex, address[] responders) external view returns (uint64);
function getIdentityRegistry() external view returns (address);                               // 0xbc4d861b
```

### Who must sign what for feedback to be accepted

**No feedbackAuth and no signature in v2.0.0.** (Older drafts had a mandatory `feedbackAuth` signed by the
agent. It was removed and does not exist in the deployed ABI.) `giveFeedback` is a plain tx from the client:
- `msg.sender` is the client (rater). Feedback is keyed by `(agentId, msg.sender)`.
- The tx reverts with `"Self-feedback not allowed"` if `msg.sender` is the agent's owner, an approved-for-all
  operator, or the token-approved address (checked via `IdentityRegistry.isAuthorizedOrOwner`).
  **So the agent's owner wallet cannot rate its own agent. The rater must be a different address.**
- It reverts with `ERC721NonexistentToken(agentId)` if the agent doesn't exist.
- It reverts with `"too many decimals"` if `valueDecimals > 18`, and `"value too large"` if `|value| > 1e38`.
- `feedbackIndex` is 1-based per (agentId, client) and increments on each call. Only the original client can revoke.
- Anti-spam is entirely the reader's job: `getSummary` **reverts with `"clientAddresses required"`** if the
  array is empty. Pass the set of client addresses you trust (e.g. TaskPay's escrow/payer addresses);
  `getClients(agentId)` lists everyone who rated.

### getSummary semantics

It averages non-revoked feedback from the given clients. A filter tag of `""` matches everything. Values are normalised to
18 decimals, averaged, then rescaled to the **most common** `valueDecimals` among the matching entries.
For example, three entries of 90, 80, 100 with decimals 0 give `(3, 90, 0)`. Gas grows with the total number of entries,
so keep it to view calls only.

Events:
```solidity
event NewFeedback(uint256 indexed agentId, address indexed clientAddress, uint64 feedbackIndex, int128 value,
    uint8 valueDecimals, string indexed indexedTag1, string tag1, string tag2, string endpoint,
    string feedbackURI, bytes32 feedbackHash);
// topic0 0x6a4a61743519c9d648a14e6493f47dbe3ff1aa29e7785c96c8326a205e58febc
event FeedbackRevoked(uint256 indexed agentId, address indexed clientAddress, uint64 indexed feedbackIndex);
// topic0 0x25156fd3288212246d8b008d5921fde376c71ed14ac2e072a506eb06fde6d09d
event ResponseAppended(uint256 indexed agentId, address indexed clientAddress, uint64 feedbackIndex,
    address indexed responder, string responseURI, bytes32 responseHash);
// topic0 0xb1c6be0b5b8aef6539e2fac0fd131a2faa7b49edf8e505b5eb0ad487d56051d4
```

## What is deployed on Monad (checked via RPC 2026-10-10)

Both chains use the same proxy pattern: an OZ `ERC1967Proxy` (Sourcify name
`project/contracts/ERC1967Proxy.sol:ERC1967Proxy`, solc 0.8.24) pointing at a UUPS
implementation. The implementation slot is the standard EIP-1967 slot
`0x360894a13ba1a3210667c828492db98dca3e2076cc3735a920a3ca505d382bbc`.
(The slot ending in `...cc7453e8ddb6ad3f6e0a0f86` returns 0. It is not the EIP-1967 slot.)

|---|---|---|
| IdentityRegistry proxy | `0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432` | `0x8004A818BFB912233c491871b3d84c89A494BD9e` |
| ReputationRegistry proxy | `0x8004BAa17C55a88189AE136b182e5fdA19dE9b63` | `0x8004B663056A597Dffe9eCcC1965A193B7388713` |
| ValidationRegistry proxy | n/a | `0x8004Cb1BF31DAf7788923b405b754f57acEB4272` (impl `0xdb31f5d9...7f99`) |
| Identity impl | `0x7274e874CA62410a93Bd8bf61c69d8045E399c02` | same address, identical bytecode |
| Reputation impl | `0x16e0FA7f7C56B9a767E34B192B51f921BE31dA34` | same address, identical bytecode |
| owner() (both proxies) | `0x547289319C3e6aedB179C0b8e8aF0B5ACd062603` | same |
| Reputation `getIdentityRegistry()` (slot 0) | `0x8004A169...a432` | `0x8004A818...BD9e` |
| Identity `_lastId` (agents registered) | 0x2858 = 10328 | 0x834 = 2100 |

The 0x8004A169/0x8004BAa1 pair is the **mainnet** vanity set. The 0x8004A818/0x8004B663 pair is
the **testnet** vanity set (same as Sepolia, Base Sepolia, etc.). Both sets were deployed via CREATE2
through the Safe singleton factory `0x914d7Fec6aaC8cd542e72Bca78B30650d45643d7` with different
placeholder salts. Implementations use salts 0x..05 (identity) and 0x..06 (reputation), which is why
the impl addresses are the same on every chain.

**Implication for TaskPay:** use a per-chain address map. The ABI is identical on both networks.
No self-deployment is needed.

## Upgradeability / initializer requirements (for a self-deploy, if ever needed)

- Both impl constructors call `_disableInitializers()`, so they take no constructor args.
- `IdentityRegistryUpgradeable.initialize()` is `reinitializer(2) onlyOwner`.
- `ReputationRegistryUpgradeable.initialize(address identityRegistry_)` is `reinitializer(2) onlyOwner`.
- Because the initializers are `onlyOwner` at version 2, **you cannot point a fresh proxy straight at
  the real impl**. Owner must first be set by a version-1 placeholder (`HardhatMinimalUUPS.initialize`,
  which runs `__Ownable_init(msg.sender)`). After that, upgrade with `upgradeToAndCall`.
- `ReputationRegistry` stores `_identityRegistry` in plain slot 0. The placeholder writes the same slot.
- Upgrade authority: `owner()` via `_authorizeUpgrade(...) onlyOwner`.

Self-deploy order (testnet, for reference only; the official one already exists):
1. Deploy `HardhatMinimalUUPS` impl (no args) → `M`.
2. Deploy `ERC1967Proxy(M, abi.encodeCall(HardhatMinimalUUPS.initialize, (address(0))))` → `IdP` (owner = deployer EOA).
3. Deploy `ERC1967Proxy(M, abi.encodeCall(HardhatMinimalUUPS.initialize, (IdP)))` → `RepP`.
4. Deploy `IdentityRegistryUpgradeable` impl (no args) → `IdI`; deploy `ReputationRegistryUpgradeable` impl → `RepI`.
5. As owner: `IdP.upgradeToAndCall(IdI, abi.encodeCall(IdentityRegistryUpgradeable.initialize, ()))`.
6. As owner: `RepP.upgradeToAndCall(RepI, abi.encodeCall(ReputationRegistryUpgradeable.initialize, (IdP)))`.
7. Check: `IdP.name()=="AgentIdentity"`, `IdP.getVersion()=="2.0.0"`, `RepP.getIdentityRegistry()==IdP`.

18 decimals, averaged, then rescaled to the **most common** `valueDecimals` among the matching entries.
For example, three entries of 90, 80, 100 with decimals 0 give `(3, 90, 0)`. Gas grows with the total number of entries,
so keep it to view calls only.
